# `jouet http`

- **Usage:** `jouet http [FLAGS] <METHOD> <URL>`

Send an HTTP request and print the status and only the JSON paths asked for, within a budget

Prints the status, the content type, size and time, the headers worth acting on (location, retry-after, rate limits), and the body cut to --budget bytes with a marker naming what was left out and the file the whole body is saved in. With --select, it prints only the values at those JSONPaths (RFC 9535) instead of the body, so nothing needs piping through jq or Python. JSON is printed compact for agents and indented for people.

--expect checks the response in hurl's style: a query (`status`, `header NAME`, `jsonpath PATH`, `body`, `duration` in milliseconds), an optional `count` and `not`, then a predicate (`==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `matches`, `exists`, `isEmpty`) and its value. Without a `status` assertion, a status of 400 or more fails.

Secrets are never printed: Authorization, cookies, and headers and JSON keys named like a token, password, API key or session are redacted, and so is any value of `${NAME}`, which jouet expands from its own environment in the URL, headers and an inline body. Give credentials that way, from the environment or through `fnox exec -- jouet http ...`, not written into the command; in a project that uses fnox, its secrets' values are redacted too.

Exits 1 when an assertion fails, 3 when a --data or --json-body file is missing, 4 when a `${NAME}` is not set, 5 when the server cannot be reached, and 124 when it does not answer within --timeout.

Examples:
  jouet http GET https://api.github.com/repos/jdx/mise --select '$.stargazers_count'
  jouet http GET localhost:3000/health --expect 'jsonpath $.ok == true'
  jouet http POST https://api.example.com/items --json-body '{"name":"x"}' --expect status=201
  fnox exec -- jouet http GET https://api.example.com/me -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${API_TOKEN}'

## Arguments
- **`<METHOD>`** — GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or OPTIONS
- **`<URL>`** — The URL; one without a scheme is taken as http:// for localhost and https:// otherwise

## Flags
- **`-H --header <NAME:VALUE>`** — A request header, NAME:VALUE (repeatable)
- **`--json-body <JSON>`** — Send JSON (checked to be JSON) with Content-Type: application/json; @FILE reads it from a file
- **`-d --data <DATA>`** — Send this text as the body; @FILE reads a file and @- stdin
- **`-s --select <JSONPATH>`** — Print only the values at this JSONPath, such as `$.items[*].name` (repeatable)
- **`-e --expect <ASSERTION>`** — Check the response, as in `status == 200` or `jsonpath $.ok == true`, and exit 1 if it fails (repeatable)
- **`--budget <BYTES>`** — The most bytes of body or selected values to print (default 4000; 0 is no limit)
- **`-i --headers`** — Print every response header, not only those worth acting on
- **`--no-follow`** — Do not follow redirects, so a 3xx is the answer
- **`--timeout <DUR>`** — Give up after DUR, such as 10s or 2m (default 30s)
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
